approach: The plane must head upwind of north so that the wind's eastward push is cancelled by a westward component of its airspeed, leaving a net northward velocity.

steps.text: Let θ be the angle west of north the pilot heads; the westward component of airspeed must cancel the eastward wind.
Find the resulting northward component of velocity.
Find the time to cover 1000 km at this northward speed.

final_answer.value: (a) the pilot should head about 23.6° west of north. (b) time taken ≈ 2.18 h (about 2 h 11 min).

common_mistakes.text: Adding the airspeed and wind speed directly to get a resultant of 700 km/h, giving a wrong time of 1000/700 ≈ 1.43 h.
Ignoring the wind entirely and using the plane's airspeed alone, giving time = 1000/500 = 2 h.
